payload.comment_body:
## Build Update

Implemented and committed the repository-owned Faktorial build contract in `74707bcf02f4b1ec1db823a3423111422eaecd60`. `Makefile` and `make.cmd` now expose aligned `worktree`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, and sequential fail-fast `quality` entry points. Worktree setup requires and quotes `FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH`; Windows uses `call` and explicit exit propagation.

Pages CI now runs `make quality` after its existing deterministic `npm ci`. Artifact upload, deployment ordering, permissions, Node 20 configuration, package scripts, and application behavior are unchanged. README documents canonical Unix/macOS and Windows commands.

Retained baseline from investigation: `npm ci`, typecheck, 69 active test files/701 tests, and all three Vite entry builds passed on the assigned clean head. Build-stage static evidence: GNU Make parsed the target contract; `git diff --check` passed; missing `FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH` and an unsupported Windows target each emitted actionable guidance and exited 2. Per stage rules, the full adapter quality/worktree commands were not pre-run and are requested from Faktorial's canonical verifier.

No Faktorial Runtime Notes were present. No UI areas, generated assets, screenshots, ADRs, rules, or custom proof declarations apply.

pull_request_description.delivered_outcome: The repository now provides one cross-platform Faktorial build contract for preparing fresh worktrees and verifying the shippable application, with matching Unix/macOS and Windows commands and the same gate used by Pages CI.
pull_request_description.implementation_approach: Added a portable `Makefile` and a repository-root `make.cmd` with aligned worktree, typecheck, test, build, and quality targets. Worktree setup performs deterministic `npm ci` in the explicitly supplied, quoted checkout path. Quality runs typecheck, the complete Vitest command, and the three-entry Vite build sequentially with failure propagation. The Pages workflow now calls `make quality`, and README documents both platform entry points.
pull_request_description.solution_rationale: Thin adapters preserve the established npm scripts as the source of each individual operation while giving Faktorial, contributors, and CI a stable repository-owned orchestration boundary. This keeps application behavior and dependency versions untouched and makes setup and verification semantics explicit across platforms.
pull_request_description.tradeoffs_and_alternatives: The small amount of orchestration is duplicated between GNU Make and Windows batch so Faktorial can invoke a native repository-root adapter on Windows without requiring GNU Make. Moving orchestration into a new Node script was considered unnecessary because the existing npm commands already define the work; the adapters only sequence them and preserve failures. CI intentionally retains its explicit `npm ci` before `make quality`, keeping dependency installation separate from routine verification while the dedicated worktree target serves fresh checkouts.
pull_request_description.architectural_decisions:
The verification process now has a repository-owned cross-platform boundary shared by local contributors, Faktorial, and Pages CI; no application architecture changed.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Unix and macOS contributors] --> M[Makefile quality]
  W[Windows contributors and Faktorial] --> C[make.cmd quality]
  P[Pages build job] --> M
  M --> Q[Typecheck then tests then production build]
  C --> Q
```
pull_request_description.verification: The retained clean-head baseline passed npm installation, typecheck, 69 active Vitest files with 701 passing tests, and all three Vite entry builds. Build-stage checks confirmed GNU Make target parsing, clean staged whitespace, and Windows exit-code-2 behavior for missing worktree configuration and unknown targets. Canonical `run-quality` verification is requested and pending; it owns execution of the new worktree and quality adapters.

verification.reason: Commit 74707bc provides the complete cross-platform adapter, CI, and documentation capability with clean static checks and verified Windows error behavior; canonical execution is required for final acceptance.
verification.handoff: If the gate fails, inspect the failing Makefile or make.cmd target and preserve the existing npm scripts, Node 20 Pages behavior, quoted FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH semantics, and nonzero exit propagation while repairing only this build-contract scope.
